::: {#exm-map-filter}
#### `map` and `filter`

Racket's `(list 1 2 3)` makes the list of 1, 2 and 3, which Racket prints as `'(1 2 3)`.
Two built-in higher-order functions (@def-higher-order) work on lists:

- `(map f L)` applies `f` to each element of the list `L`, and returns the list of results.
  With `add-three` from @exr-twice, `(map add-three (list 1 2 3))` returns `'(4 5 6)`.
- `(filter p L)` returns the list of the elements `x` of `L` for which `(p x)` is true.
  `(filter even? (list 1 2 3 4 5 6))` returns `'(2 4 6)`.

Neither one changes `L`; each returns a new list.

:::
